title: QuizMaster shared definitions
description: Reusable definitions for every en-te-hi data file. Nothing here is a standalone document; refer to it with $ref from the per-file schemas.

languageCode.description: Display languages supported by the app. 'en' is always the language being taught; 'te' and 'hi' are support languages.

localizedText.description: A single string in all three languages. All three keys are required so the renderer never has to fall back.

localizedList.description: Parallel string arrays, one per language. INVARIANT (checked by tools/validate_data.py, not expressible in JSON Schema): en, te and hi must have identical length, and index i must refer to the same item in all three languages.

classList.description: Classes an entry is appropriate for. Source entries may serve several grades (a Class 5 word is still usable for Class 6 revision); a generator selects entries with `classes.includes(selectedClass)`.

tags.description: Free-form lowercase filter tags. Difficulty is carried here too ('beginner' | 'intermediate' | 'advanced') to match the existing tag filter UI.

category.description: Fixed taxonomy. The `category` of a question must be one of these exactly; source entries carry a `categoryHint` used to stamp generated questions.

register.description: Formality band. Feeds the 'Formal vs Informal English' category.

envelope.description: Header fields common to every data file. Per-file schemas add their own payload array on top of these.

schemaVersion.description: Semver of the schema this file conforms to. Bump the major when a loader change is required.

fieldSelector.description: Tells a generator where to read option text from inside a source entry.

path.description: Property name on the entry holding a localizedText (e.g. 'word', 'meaning') or a localizedList (e.g. 'synonyms').

pick.description: How to reduce a localizedList to one item. Ignored for localizedText paths. 'index' uses the `index` property.

display.description: Maps each DISPLAY column to the SOURCE language read from the entry. Default is identity ({en:en, te:te, hi:hi}). Use a constant source (e.g. all three set to 'en') when the option text is an English artefact that must not be translated, such as a sentence being corrected.

generatorSpec.description: A declarative recipe turning one source entry into one question object shaped exactly like an entry in en-te-hi-questions.json. Template tokens are written as {{path.lang}} (e.g. {{word.en}}, {{headword.te}}); {{answer}} resolves to the correct option text in the column being rendered.

oneOf.description: Per-entry generator: one source entry becomes one question.
Aggregate generator: several source entries become one question.

id.description: Stable generator id. Generated question ids are `<idPrefix>-<generator.id>-<entry.id>` so a regenerated bank is stable and de-duplicable.

requires.description: Entry fields that must be present for an entry to be the SUBJECT of a generated question. Lets a generator depend on optional fields (cloze, situation, formalEquivalent) without those fields becoming mandatory for every entry. This does not restrict distractors: an entry is eligible as a distractor whenever it has the field named by `distractors.from.path`.

weight.description: Relative frequency when the generator has more entries than the requested question count.

distractors.description: Where wrong options come from. Required for mcq and flip-card; omit for true-false.

scope.description: 'self' draws the wrong options from the same entry (e.g. an antonym list); 'siblings' draws from other entries in the same file.

poolFallback.description: What to do when the preferred pool holds fewer than `count` usable distractors — the normal case for a small class-tagged file. 'widen' walks the ladder same-class -> adjacent class (+/-1) -> any class in the file, stopping as soon as `count` distractors are available. 'strict' never widens and the generator instead skips the entry. Either way a generator MUST NOT emit a question with fewer options than count+1.

falseStatement.description: true-false generators only: template for the deliberately wrong variant. The generator emits the true form or this false form at random and sets correctAnswer accordingly.

aggregate.description: match-pairs and drag-drop only: build ONE question out of several entries rather than one question per entry. The generator picks `count` eligible entries, reads `left` from each to build the left column and `right` to build the right column, shuffles the right column, and records the resulting index pairs in correctAnswer. Mutually exclusive with `answer`/`distractors`.

minCount.description: Fewest pairs worth asking. If the class does not have `count` eligible entries the generator widens to adjacent classes and then to the whole file; if it still falls short it emits a smaller question down to `minCount`, and below that emits nothing.
